key_insight: Diamond color defects are promising quantum-network nodes because they combine strong optical interfaces, fast spin control, and long coherence times.
engineering_relevance: The review highlights a path toward scalable quantum hardware by integrating diamond nanophotonics with photonic integrated circuits for distributed quantum communication and processing.
method: Survey optical and spin properties of diamond color defects for network-node design.
Review recent progress in quantum-network building blocks and metropolitan-scale demonstrations.
Discuss integration strategies and remaining experimental/fundamental challenges.
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes prior demonstrations and system advances rather than reporting new experimental data or a single benchmark evaluation.
watch_item: Scalability still depends on overcoming material, fabrication, and heterogeneous-integration challenges at both the device and system levels.
paper_title: Quantum Networks Using Color Defects in Diamond: Principles, Progress, and Perspectives
